visualReview.notes: Connected Brooklyn Museum exterior: long pale stone wings and asymmetric rear ranges, six tapered Ionic columns with abstract volutes and real colonnade depth, supported triangular pediment/original geometric relief, square attic and shallow stone dome, repeated tall window proxies/pilasters/cornices and flat roof skylights. Five descending concentric glass-roof bands form the curved entrance pavilion with metal framing, a real 1.1m lower entrance recess/soffit/threshold and two short approach treads. The picture-led rear court stays open. Moved the frontal camera onto the plaza after procedural buildings across the street obscured it. Ordinary front photograph/aerial and standard PMTiles/Mapzen guided one continuous author/inspect/fix pass. Temporary banners, copied sculptures/inscriptions, terrace gardens/fountains and furnished rooms remain outside scope.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Seven material roles share six existing 256px graphs: stone_limestone (wall/trim tint variants), plaster_lime (court), membrane, storefront (opaque window/glass-roof proxies), metal_painted and brick. Canonical metric UVs, sRGB-to-linear tint and baked graph means for skyline. Seven textured draws/one skyline; no embedded image, private atlas or new graph. Separate vertex streams and equal CPU/GPU accounting. Every used graph reads once, and unloading disposes all model geometry. Native grade-specific bases intersect flat review planes or expose patches; original native terrain supplies geographic fit.

Skyline simplifies the stepped pavilion roof to one glass cap while keeping the six-column portico, attic/dome and open rear court. Every LOD keeps both approach treads. Four LODs/failure/unload preserve1326 resident /1864 wider independent buildings, original201x201/6m terrain, roads and9087.535m² water. Failure keeps all1328 original resident buildings. Every run restores ground/water and leaves zero live model geometry. Default synthetic street context frames place the camera inside the rear court and clip a roof underside at the upper edge; custom front/detail frames and the current native exterior views cover the portico, pavilion, entrances, wings and open court.

limitations: Connected Brooklyn Museum exterior: exact parent/part footprint, long pale Beaux-Arts wings and rear ranges, picture-led open rear court, six-column Ionic portico/recessed upper doorway, supported triangular pediment and abstract relief/roof ornament, square attic and shallow stone dome, flat roof/skylights and the curved stepped glass entrance pavilion. Pavilion has a real central recessed lower door, soffit and threshold; glass is an opaque reflected exterior proxy. Outer terraced landscape, fountains, garden collections, temporary exhibition banners, freestanding art, furnished rooms and copied sculpture/inscriptions remain outside this model. Two short exterior treads bridge the approximate 0.4m native threshold grade.
